title: if as an Expression
hints: Since Swift 5.9, `if` can be an expression that produces a value.
Compute the BMI, then write `let category = if … { "…" } else if … { "…" } else { "…" }`.
`let bmi = weightKg / (heightM * heightM)` and the chain `< 18.5`, `< 25`, `< 30`, else "obese".
jsBridge: Swift 5.9 made `if` and `switch` **expressions**, so `let x = if … { a } else { b }` works like a multi-branch ternary. JS has nothing equivalent without an IIFE or a chain of nested ternaries.

compass.q: JS devs nest ternaries or use IIFEs for this. What makes Swift's version type-safe that the IIFE isn't?
